_comment: Maintained rate table, dollars per MILLION tokens, keyed by model id.
Rates go stale. They live here rather than in code so updating them is a
data edit, and so a page can state which day its figures were checked.
Cache writes bill at a multiple of base input: 1.25x on the 5-minute TTL,
2x on the 1-hour TTL. Cache reads bill at `cache_read_multiple` times base
input, 0.1x when a row omits it. The published exceptions carry their own
value on the row (Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 at 0.025x, Opus 5.5 at 0.05x) so
the fact lives here once and the test and the page note both read it.
The 1M context window carries no premium, so every `[1m]` alias prices off
its base row.
Reasoning tokens are a SUBSET of output tokens and bill at the output rate.
They are never a separate line item; see cost.REASONING_IS_SUBSET_OF_OUTPUT.
`unpriced` lists models that really do appear in transcripts but have no
Anthropic list price: locally hosted models, models reached through a
routed backend, and the harness's own synthetic messages. A session on one
of these renders with the cost figures suppressed and a note saying why.
An UNKNOWN model renders the same way, and the CLI also prints a warning,
because a missing entry means the table needs updating. Unknown means a
model that is in neither list AND could carry Anthropic list rates, which
cost.is_unknown decides from provider_for rather than a second list here.
`providers` names who served each model. Transcripts record no provider,
base URL, or endpoint, so this is inferred from the model id and nothing
else. Every model under `models` is Anthropic without needing an entry;
unpriced models are listed explicitly. Which Ollama HOST served a session
is not recoverable and is never guessed: the provider is as far as it goes.

unpriced.<synthetic>: a harness-generated message, not an API call
unpriced.glm-4.7-flash: runs locally through Ollama, so no per-token price applies
unpriced.qwen3:30b-a3b: runs locally through Ollama, so no per-token price applies
unpriced.openai/gpt-5.6-sol: reached through a routed non-Anthropic backend
